sub.en: Look at the sentences. Where does the frequency word go — before or after the verb? And what changes after be?

items.q: He ___ at six.
items.why: One-word frequency adverbs go before the main verb.

items.q: She ___ late.
items.why: …but after am / is / are: she is never late.

items.q: They ___ go out in the week.
I go to the gym ___.
items.why: A frequency phrase (twice a week, every day) goes at the end, not before the verb.

items.q: ___, I check my to-do list.
items.why: A frequency phrase can also open the sentence, for emphasis.

items.q: My sister ___ the housework every Sunday.
He ___ chess — he says it’s too slow.
“How often ___ you go camping?” — “About once a year.”

acts.title: A day in three lives
text: THE NIGHT NURSE. Aigul starts work at eight in the evening and finishes at eight in the morning, four nights a week. She hardly ever sees daylight in winter. She always eats her main meal at two in the morning, which she says is the strangest part of the job. On her days off she sleeps until midday and then does two weeks of housework in one afternoon.

THE FREELANCER. Dana works from home and makes a to-do list every morning. In theory her hours are equal to everybody else’s; in practice she often works until nine and then feels guilty for stopping. She goes running twice a week and plays chess online with a stranger in Poland almost every night. She says she never stays in on Friday, but her friends say she usually does.

THE FARMER. Marat is outdoors from six until dark. His week has no weekend in it: the animals eat on Sunday too. He goes to town once a month, plays cards with his brothers about twice a year, and has never been camping in his life — “Why would I sleep outside? I already live outside.”

tts: So Maria, what’s this book about? — Well, it’s about running, but it’s also about Murakami’s life. He talks about why running and writing are important to him.
And why is running important to him? — He says it helps him think. He runs about ten kilometres a day, six days a week, and he has done it for more than twenty years.
Does he ever take a day off? — One day a week. He says that if he stops for longer, it becomes difficult to start again.

write.q: Describe your typical week: 6 sentences. Use two one-word frequency adverbs, two frequency phrases, and one sentence about a person with he or she.
write.model: I usually get up at half past six and I always check my to-do list before breakfast. I go to the gym twice a week, on Tuesday and Friday. I hardly ever go out during the week, but I see my sister every Sunday. My flatmate does the housework about once a month, which is a problem. He is never late for anything else.

speak.q: Answer out loud: How often do you exercise? What do you always do in the morning? What do you hardly ever do? Then describe one other person’s week.
speak.model: I go running twice a week. I always check my emails before breakfast. I hardly ever go to the cinema. My sister works four nights a week and sleeps until midday on her days off.
